title: CVE-2026-68820: Actively Exploited Windows AFD.sys Zero-Day Enables SYSTEM Privilege Escalation
content_md: Microsoft’s August 2026 Patch Tuesday addresses hundreds of security vulnerabilities, but one issue stands out because attackers were already exploiting it before a fix became available. CVE-2026-68820 is a high-severity elevation-of-privilege vulnerability in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock, or AFD.sys, that can allow a local attacker to escalate privileges to SYSTEM. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 7.0 and resides in a core Windows kernel driver responsible for supporting socket operations used by the Windows Sockets API. Although exploitation requires an attacker to already have code running on the target machine, successful abuse effectively turns an existing foothold into full system-level control without requiring additional user interaction. The vulnerability has also been linked to real-world nation-state activity. Check Point Research attributed exploitation to the North Korea-linked Lazarus group as part of its long-running Operation Dream Job campaign, where attackers used the zero-day to deploy a new version of the FudModule kernel-mode rootkit after initially compromising targeted systems. CVE-2026-68820 analysis At a technical level, CVE-2026-68820 is a use-after-free vulnerability in AFD.sys caused by improper synchronization when multiple threads interact with socket-related state concurrently.
